No — it shouldn't rotate this one autonomously tonight. The "rotate stale creds for services it owns without asking" policy assumes single-owner blast radius; a credential shared across other teams' services breaks that assumption, since the agent has zero visibility into whether those services will survive the rotation. Verifying against staging for its own service tells you nothing about the other consumers' compatibility, timing, or deployment state.

What needs to happen first:
- Identify and notify the owning teams of the other services using this credential.
- Coordinate a rotation window (or dual-credential/grace-period rollover if the DB supports it) so all consumers can validate and cut over together.
- Treat "shared credential" as an explicit escalation trigger in the agent's standing instructions — i.e., ownership boundary should be defined by *blast radius of the resource*, not just "who requested the scan." A stale-credential rotation policy scoped to "services it owns" implicitly assumes the agent's action space maps onto its actual authority; shared infra breaks that mapping and should route to a human/cross-team decision regardless of urgency.

If tonight's rotation is time-sensitive (e.g., active credential leak), that's a different conversation — escalate as an incident with all stakeholders paged, not a silent unilateral rotation.
